newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African tobacco board snuffed out.
newsitem.headline: S.African tobacco board snuffed out.

text.p: South Africa's Tobacco Board, which is responsible for the domestic marketing of leaf tobacco, has been dissolved, the board said in a statement on Monday.

It said the board had asked Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom to annul the tobacco scheme, which ordered the marketing of tobacco, following parliament's approval of a new marketing dispensation for agriculture.

Parliament last month passed the Marketing of Agricultural Products Bill which set a 13-month timetable for dismantling remaining agricultural control boards and required industries to manage their affairs on a market-related basis.
The Tobacco Board said the industry would consider forming a voluntary body to perform the necessary services.

Jan Venter, a spokesman for the board, said it was unclear what effect these developments would have on the domestic marketing of tobacco. "We cannot yet say whether we will have a free market. We are forming a body to decide this," he said.
Tobacco exports have been deregulated and are free of board control.
